profile.address: 7, Teleport Drive, Staten Island, Richmond County, New York, 10314
profile.reading:
Telehouse's New York Teleport facility occupies a 162,000 square foot building at 7 Teleport Drive on the West Shore of Staten Island, inside an office and telecommunications park that took its name from its original purpose as a satellite teleport serving the New York region. The Teleport park was developed in the 1980s around satellite earth station infrastructure meant to give New York area broadcasters and carriers direct access to satellite uplinks, and the Telehouse building was one of the first facilities there to anchor that development with a fiber and colocation offering rather than a purely satellite based one. The building opened in 1989, making it one of the longest continuously operating carrier and colocation facilities in the New York metropolitan market, predating most of the purpose built data centers that now cluster in New Jersey and around Manhattan's core network meet me points. It has operated throughout under the Telehouse brand, a data center and network services company that is a subsidiary of Japan's KDDI Corporation and runs a global chain of facilities built around telecommunications carrier neutrality.

Telehouse's own materials for the site describe standby power as six diesel generators totaling 5,625 kVA, configured N plus 1, a sizable backup generation base for a building of this footprint. The same materials separately state that 10 megawatts of total power is available at the facility and that individual cabinets can be provisioned up to a maximum of 20 kilowatts, though the published materials do not make clear whether either figure represents power currently drawn by tenants, capacity reserved for future growth, or simply a ceiling on what a single cabinet could be provisioned to rather than a typical operating density. This profile reports them as published figures rather than confirmed operating loads. Telehouse does not publish current occupancy, a named tenant list, or any third party facility certification, such as an Uptime Institute tier rating, for the New York Teleport building.

Staten Island's relative distance from Manhattan's densest carrier hotels has historically made this facility more of a secondary interconnection point for the region than buildings located directly in lower Manhattan or across the river in New Jersey, but its age, its diesel generation capacity, and its continuous operation under one well known international operator for more than three decades make it a stable and long standing part of the New York area's telecommunications and data center landscape.

reading.body:
Telehouse Teleport's published capacity is unknown. The facility occupies a carrier-neutral colocation site in Staten Island positioned as a network hub for the northeastern United States, but the operator has not disclosed megawatts available for IT load on its public specification pages. Without a published figure, the campus cannot be ranked by capacity or assessed against AI compute density benchmarks.

New York State has 31 mapped data center facilities, of which only one publishes power capacity to this site's search. Telehouse Teleport's rank of second by published megawatts reflects the near-total absence of disclosed capacity data in the state, not a measure of its actual size or strategic importance to AI workloads. The single published figure in New York totals 3 megawatts.

The facility's market positioning emphasizes interconnection and peering rather than large-scale compute density. Telehouse operates as a subsidiary of KDDI Corporation, a major Japanese telecom, and competes in the colocation and carrier services segment. Whether Telehouse Teleport can absorb material AI training load depends on undisclosed power infrastructure, allocation policies, and available cabinet space, none of which are published.
